title: LLM Safeguards: Security Privacy Compliance Anti Hallucination: Daniel Whitenack
talk_summary: Daniel Whitenack walks through a checklist of LLM deployment risks (hallucination, supply chain, data leakage, prompt injection) and the guardrail layers Prediction Guard built around models. The most transferable ideas are cheap non-LLM classifiers/vector checks for validation and gating, plus dry-run-then-approve for agent permissions.

takeaways.technique: Small factual-consistency model instead of LLM-as-judge
takeaways.what_they_do: Score model output against ground-truth text using a fine-tuned NLP model (e.g. UniEval/BARTScore-style) rather than a second LLM call, so validation is cheap and fast.
takeaways.evidence_quote: use one of these NLP models that is much smaller it can run on CPU very performant maybe it does take like 200 milliseconds

takeaways.what_they_do: Compare incoming prompts against a curated set of known injection examples via semantic/vector search and threshold on max/average score, avoiding a model call.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can have a sort of stable of examples of prompt injections and not prompt injections ... it's an operation against a database not an operation against a model

takeaways.technique: Dry-run then human-approve for agent actions
takeaways.what_they_do: Have the agent produce a dry run of intended actions (e.g. config changes) for review/approval rather than granting broad permissions up front.
takeaways.evidence_quote: have a dry run of what the agent is going to do and then like have that approved

takeaways.technique: PII filter in front of model calls
takeaways.what_they_do: Detect PII/PHI in inputs and block, strip, or replace with fake values before the prompt reaches the model or logs.
Pull models only from a curated registry, verify hashes/attestation, and keep 'trust untrusted code' disabled.
takeaways.evidence_quote: check a hash when you pull down that model to make sure it hasn't been tampered with

takeaways.what_they_do: Make each guardrail callable individually with visible scores so operators can see why something was blocked and adjust thresholds.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if something's getting blocked right you can hit it against that model look at the scores change your thresholds
